Times New Roman's kern table (times.ttf, upem 2048) has 'space A' = -113 and 'space T' = -37 units: at 96 pt that is -5.89 px and -1.93 px, total -7.81 px, matching the measured 7.5 px width difference. Line 1 'The Restoration' has no kern pairs and its extents match exactly (86.0-720.0). Visible at normal size as a wider gap in 'Of  All'.
findings.xml_evidence: slide1.xml sp id=2 (ph ctrTitle): rPr sz=9600 spc=-300, latin typeface='Times New Roman'; no kern on the run, so kern=1200 is inherited from slideMaster1 titleStyle lvl1pPr defRPr (kerning on for >= 12 pt); algn=ctr from titleStyle.
findings.suspected_cause: Euro-Office ignores kern=1200 pair kerning for Times New Roman, at least for pairs involving the space glyph (space+A, space+T), so the spaces keep their full advance; PowerPoint applies the font's kern/GPOS pairs when the font size is >= kern threshold.

findings.xml_evidence: sp id=19 'Rectangle 18': xfrm off=(4849460,1823892) ext=(3891149,3208571); solidFill srgbClr FFFFCC; <a:ln> with only solidFill schemeClr tx1 (no w, so 9525 EMU = 0.75 pt); bodyPr spAutoFit.
findings.suspected_cause: Thin (0.75 pt = 1.67 render px) outline edges at fractional positions are rasterized with a different pixel-coverage rule. In these renders strokes are aliased (pure black). PowerPoint fills a pixel only when the stroke covers about half of it or more (pixel centre inside), so an edge centred at .4-.6 of a pixel gets 1 pixel and one centred near .0-.2 gets 2; Euro-Office also fills neighbouring pixels covered by only about 0.25-0.4, giving 3 pixels. Fix: use centre-sampling (or PowerPoint-style width rounding) for non-antialiased strokes so the outline is not widened.

Red-ink area of the Cush head 37.2 px^2 (PPT) vs 43.9 px^2 (EO), ratio 1.18; width ratio about 1.13-1.14; length 6.5 vs 7.5 px. Unlike K1 (2.25 pt lines, about 1.5x and 2-4 px overshoot), here the line is 0.75 pt and both apps are clearly applying a minimum head size (PowerPoint's head is about 8.5x the line width, Euro-Office's about 9.7x), so the error is smaller but in the same direction. Lines themselves coincide.
findings.xml_evidence: Each connector: prstGeom straightConnector1, <a:ln><a:solidFill><a:srgbClr val="FF0000"/></a:solidFill><a:tailEnd type="triangle"/></a:ln> (no w/len, so med/med; no ln w, so width from <a:lnRef idx="1"> = theme lnStyleLst[0] w=9525 EMU = 0.75 pt); flipV or flipH on xfrm (e.g. connector 9: xfrm flipV off 2405232,3633109 ext 465424x457199).
findings.suspected_cause: Euro-Office's line-end size for thin lines uses a larger minimum or a different base width than PowerPoint (PowerPoint seems to size the head from roughly 2 pt for lines thinner than that; Euro-Office from about 2.2 pt) and positions the tip beyond the end point instead of on it. Probably the same arrowhead-sizing/placement code as K1, but the fix must also reproduce PowerPoint's thin-line minimum.

Euro-Office tip at y 126.2 (3.8 px beyond the end point), base at y 148.0 (1.5 px further down the shaft), base width 21.5-22 px (x 129.0-151.0 vs 132.0-148.0): about 1.3x the specified size. The flank slope is the same in both (width grows 1 px per 1 px of length), so the shape is right but grown on every side by half the line width. Stroking the 16.7 x 16.7 triangle with the 3.33-px pen (mitred) predicts exactly this: tip +(w/2)/sin(26.6 deg) = +3.7 px, base +1.67 px, base width 16.7 + w/cos(26.6 deg) + 1.67 = 22.1 px. The same arithmetic on the K1 case (2.25 pt line, med/med = 7.5 px triangle) gives 11.5 px width and 2.8 px overshoot, matching K1, so this is the K1 mechanism at lg/lg size (1.3x rather than 1.5x because the added w is a smaller fraction of a 5w head). Region 4 (134 px, all only in Euro-Office).

findings.suspected_cause: Different pixel snapping/rounding of the outline rectangle's bottom edge (fractional device-row position) in Euro-Office's stroke rasterization.
findings.rejected_reason: Not a Euro-Office error. The outline has an explicit w=9525, and Euro-Office's PDF strokes the exact geometry (rect bottom at PDF y 140.24523 pt, width 0.74999). PowerPoint's own PDF export rounds the rect origin to 0.01 pt ('132.75 140.25 459 29.081 re'). That 0.0048 pt (0.01 device px) shift puts the stroke edge exactly on a device-pixel centre, so the shared Windows.Data.Pdf rasterizer lights row 887 for PowerPoint and not for Euro-Office. This is rounding in the reference PDF at a pixel-centre tie, not a rendering rule Euro-Office could fix.

findings.powerpoint: The italic 'Explanation: ...' paragraph (9 lines, y 352.5-509.5) starts a little lower below 'Isaiah 22:20-24'; first line centroid y 358.77.
findings.euro_office: The whole italic paragraph is shifted up: first line centroid y 358.04, last line 502.02 vs 502.77; every one of its 9 lines is 0.6-0.75 px higher, while all 11 lines above it match to 0.03 px.
findings.detail: Cross-correlation (drift.py) gives dy -0.61 px constant along the first and last italic lines (x 110-700), dy 0.00 on the bold 'Isaiah 22:20-24' line directly above. Line pitch inside the paragraph is identical (18.04 vs 18.05 px), so only the gap before the paragraph differs: baseline-to-baseline from 'Isaiah' to the first italic line is about 23.0 px in Euro-Office (18.0 px line pitch + 5.0 px = exactly 4.5 pt) and about 23.6 px in PowerPoint. Glyph shapes are the same Calibri Italic in both (crop 0837-1). This is the only paragraph on slides 835-838 with spcBef, and the only one that moved.
findings.xml_evidence: slide837.xml sp id=7 'Rectangle 6': bodyPr wrap=square, spAutoFit, default insets; 4th <a:p> has <a:pPr><a:spcBef><a:spcPts val="450"/></a:spcBef></a:pPr> and a run rPr sz=1350 i=1; previous paragraph is a b=1 run 'Isaiah 22:20-24' with endParaRPr sz=1350 i=1. No lnSpc anywhere; presentation defaultTextStyle has no spcBef. Calibri, Calibri Bold and Calibri Italic have identical vertical metrics (hhea 1536/-512/452, win 1950/550), so the font face does not explain the shift.
findings.suspected_cause: Euro-Office converts spcBef spcPts 450 to a gap about 0.55 pt (0.6 px) smaller than PowerPoint's; PowerPoint's effective space before appears to be about 5.05 pt rather than 4.5 pt (possibly PowerPoint adds spcBef in a different unit or rounds the paragraph position), so Euro-Office's point-to-px conversion or rounding of space-before should be checked.
